ranked.headline: Spatial and single-cell methods separate technical artifacts from biological variation
ranked.summary: New preprints model transcript spillover, contamination, label uncertainty and prediction confidence in spatial and single-cell transcriptomics.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit modeling of technical error in spatial and single-cell transcriptomics. In imaging-based platforms, Dancer uses a reference-guided probabilistic framework to separate within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination. SYNDRI, a transformer trained on simulated data, removes transcript spillover. SLUICE (R/Seurat) uses screening label uncertainty to separate robust from fragile cell-type composition changes in Xenium data after TBI. For histology-to-expression inference, REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence and reports gains in cell-type annotation and prognostic value in TCGA-BRCA. A noise-corrected correlation metric (RSC) is proposed for benchmarking such models. Adjacent work addresses data fidelity more broadly: benchmarking of sample-mispairing detection, scRefine's contrastive atlas integration, RecurSieve's detection of non-mean expression differences, and Tumor2Line's optimal-transport tumor–cell-line alignment. CHO transcriptome compendia, UCE state bridges and lung adenocarcinoma Global Tumor Time are peripheral. All are preprints, so reported gains are unreviewed.

ranked.headline: Splicing QTLs, perturbations and enhancer models link noncoding risk variants to genes
ranked.summary: Preprints on IBD, T2D, osteoarthritis and alcohol use disorder go beyond expression QTLs to splicing, allelic chromatin, MPRA and enhancer-gene benchmarks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is assigning disease-associated noncoding variants to effector genes in relevant tissues or cell types, increasingly beyond total transcript abundance. Joint colon eQTL and sQTL mapping in 1,149 IBD samples finds GWAS-colocalized expression and splicing effects implicating NMD and immune pathways. Colocalization of 338 fine-mapped T2D signals with adipose expression, splicing and transcript usage identifies RNA features missed by expression alone. Pangenome genotyping of 645,680 structural variants in CARTaGENE yields 103 SV-eQTLs. Mechanistic follow-up appears at individual loci: MPRA and CRISPR perturbation in chondrocytes link rs1895062 to PAPPA, and microglial allele-specific accessibility shows rs7307261 alters ETS-factor binding. Methods target the enhancer-gene step directly: CREMAP adjusts latent factors before peak-gene testing in single-cell multiome data, E2GScore benchmarks sequence-to-function models, and EPIC2 maps traits to cell types from single-cell accessibility. The IGVF Catalog integrates 657 datasets as shared infrastructure.

ranked.headline: Foundation model embeddings for single-cell and spatial data face scrutiny and repurposing
ranked.summary: New preprints dissect what transcriptomic foundation model features encode and test frozen embeddings for imputation, translation and cytokine-response tasks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is examining and reusing learned representations of gene expression rather than reporting accuracy alone. Sparse autoencoders applied to transcriptomic foundation models yield concept-labeled features that largely behave as gene detectors on spatial panels. A separate test shows a 4-D value track and simple encodings retain most performance in single-cell foundation models, questioning 512-dimensional value embeddings for gene counts. Frozen embeddings are also being repurposed: CYTAP adapts them with baseline-relative representations to infer responses across 90 cytokines, and SimpleP2G finds Virchow2 image features with a simple frozen-embedding decoder effective for predicting expression from pathology images. A second strand handles cross-context inference: BRIDGE uses contrastive learning to impute donor-specific expression across GTEx tissues, and scXOrGAN translates single-cell transcriptomes between organs from cell-unpaired data. GASTON-VI learns spatial axes and molecular gradients from multi-sample spatial omics, and AUTOENCODIX provides a model hub benchmarked on 3.7 million human cells.

ranked.headline: Extracellular matrix and complement pathways emerge as regulators of synapses and barriers
ranked.summary: New preprints tie astrocyte Cathepsin D, NRG1/ErbB4-maintained perineuronal nets and complement to memory, synaptic plasticity and early BBB failure.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is extracellular matrix and complement signaling as control points for synaptic plasticity and neurovascular integrity. Astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D supports hippocampal LTP and memory through matrix degradation, defining an astrocyte–matrix–synapse axis. In adult mice, enriched environment increases prefrontal perineuronal nets via NRG1/ErbB4 signaling and aggrecan, with improved cognition. Aiolos (Ikzf3), dysregulated in schizophrenia patients, is expressed in hippocampal neurons and may regulate complement-mediated structural synaptic elimination. At the vascular interface, NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL iPSC endothelial and microtissue models show early BBB failure with complement–matrix activation and metabolic defects. A secondary theme is lipid and proteomic readouts in neurodegeneration: human lipidomics with humanized APOE mice identifies AD-linked lipid transport deficits that engineered lipoprotein particles target, and a cross-tissue atlas links cell-type-specific snRNA-seq changes in Parkinson's disease and MSA to biofluid EV proteomes. Culture-media effects on iPSC-neuron proteome composition and turnover are a methodological caveat for such models.

ranked.headline: Cortical, thalamic and striatal circuits shape risk-taking, threat coding and flexible choice
ranked.summary: New rodent work maps how insula, prethalamus and prelimbic cortex resolve threat-reward conflict, alongside dopamine and cerebellar roles in adaptive behavior.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how rodent circuits arbitrate behavior under threat. In an approach-avoidance task, rats occupied three latent behavioral states, and anterior insular activity tracked the active state rather than integrated outcomes, arguing that conflict is resolved by state selection. A preprint identifies inhibitory prethalamic vLGN as promoting risk-taking under threat, with opposing retrosplenial and ventromedial hypothalamic inputs shaping exploratory 'courage.' Prelimbic single units encode diverse danger-modulated behaviors and the learned probability structure of threat during probabilistic fear conditioning. A second thread concerns dopamine and flexible control. Nigral dopamine shapes dorsomedial striatal ramping, including down-ramping MSNs, during interval timing. Ventral striatal dopamine rises after hippocampal sharp-wave ripples, more strongly during offline rest and with longer, higher-power ripples. Mid-posterior cerebellar Purkinje cells encode reinforcement-learning parameters, and lobule VIa photostimulation speeds contingency adaptation. Together, the work favors state- and probability-based representations over simple outcome summation.

ranked.headline: Stressed organelles are remodeled via distinct protein-level sensors, tethers and extraction routes
ranked.summary: New preprints and one JCB paper assign specific factors to mitochondrial, ER, lysosomal and vesicular responses, from OXA1L copper sensing to VCP-dependent ER degradation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that organelle quality control and stress adaptation proceed through context-specific protein-level routes rather than one shared mechanism. OXA1L binds copper, disrupting mitoribosome assembly and releasing MRPL20 to the nucleus, where ATF5-driven UPRmt restrains cuproptosis. ATAD1 is localized to mitochondria-ER contact sites and moves mislocalized Pex26 from mitochondria to the ER. Induced ubiquitination by cytosolic E3 ligases degrades ER membrane proteins through VCP-dependent extraction, bypassing canonical ERAD. At the axon initial segment, MCF2L anchors lysosomes via gAnkG and retains less acidic ones. Munc13-4 coupling to Rab27a in mast cells governs exosome fusion pore opening after docking. A HECT E3 pSILAC screen adds UPS-wide redundancy and compensation between E3s. New here is the assignment of a defined factor to each context; a unifying mechanism is not shown.

ranked.headline: Tubulin, dynein and Hippo-linked cytoskeletal defects drive progenitor failure in developmental disease models
ranked.summary: Independent TTC5 mouse studies and variant-specific dynein organoids tie progenitor mitosis and cytoskeletal regulation to cortical malformation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is disease-variant models that trace developmental malformation to progenitor-level cytoskeletal and mitotic defects. Two Ttc5 loss-of-function mouse studies, one a knockout and one a patient nonsense mutation, converge on impaired neurogenesis, mitotic errors and disrupted tubulin homeostasis, with elevated γ-tubulin extending tubulin autoregulation to TTC5. Patient-derived cortical organoids show that dynein variants differ in their effects on spindle organization and apoptosis. A catalytically inactive TAOK1 variant in organoids enhances progenitor proliferation via impaired Hippo signaling and YAP1. Two items are related but distinct: p53-dependent mesenchymal progenitor defects in a Diamond Blackfan anemia model, and a Hippo-dystrophin axis maintaining cortical actin in Capsaspora. New here are the convergent TTC5 evidence and the variant-specific dynein comparison.

ranked.headline: Multi-omic and graph methods resolve immune cell states and interferon-alpha programs in disease
ranked.summary: Six preprints apply multi-omic, long-read and graph methods to resolve immune states, including interferon-alpha and CD40 programs in Sjögren's disease.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is computational resolution of immune heterogeneity from high-dimensional data rather than a single interferon finding. The most direct interferon item uses mGEDO to define interferon-alpha and CD40 signatures in Sjögren's disease, with distinct transcripto-methylomic profiles suggesting complementary immune programs for patient stratification. Related work resolves bystander versus tumor-specific T cells with a multimodal graph neural network integrating transcriptomes and TCR sequences, and identifies a CTLA4-high naive CD4 T cell subpopulation in aging through subsampling-based analysis. Others derive cell-type-resolved epigenetic clocks from long-read methylation data, link gene-dependency network structure in CAR T infusion products to treatment failure risk, and show that CHIP driver mutations have heterogeneous effects. Evidence is preprint-only.

ranked.headline: Clock, transcription factor and m6A regulation reshape timing and output of plant stress responses
ranked.summary: New work links CCA1/LHY, DOF/REVEILLE, MYB/AP2-ERF and m6A regulators to timing and decoupling of stress and developmental programs.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is regulatory control over when and how plants deploy stress-related programs. In Arabidopsis, CCA1 and LHY mutants alter time-of-day heat responses across transcriptome, proteome and metabolome, implicating sulfur and ROS processes. In cultivated potato, diel expression phase differs from wild Solanum species independently of clock period, with DOF and REVEILLE factors linked to the shifts. In white spruce, autumn warming decouples photosynthesis and cold-acclimation networks from growth cessation, with MYB and AP2/ERF regulators implicated. Two Plant Physiology studies add m6A-based control: MeRIP-seq and metabolomics in drought-contrasting wheat, and the cold-repressed demethylase PpALKBH9 stabilizing PpFUL4 mRNA to promote ethylene-associated peach ripening. New emphasis falls on phase shifts, program decoupling and epitranscriptomic regulation.

ranked.headline: Perturbation-response models pair interaction structure and uncertainty with standardized benchmarks
ranked.summary: New preprints define Virtual Cell Challenge metrics and model non-additive effects and label noise in siRNA, combinatorial, and CRISPRi fitness prediction.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting responses to genetic perturbation while making evaluation, interaction structure, and label reliability explicit. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 specifies six metrics for zero-shot prediction of transcriptional responses to CRISPRi knockdowns. GAIN models single-cell combinatorial responses as an additive baseline plus a learned interaction term. siGMA applies a heteroscedastic multimodal model to chemically modified siRNA efficacy, quantifying uncertainty across noisy cross-dataset labels. FluxStack couples enzyme-constrained flux landscapes with light-aware knockdown FBA to predict light-dependent CRISPRi gene fitness in Synechocystis PCC 6803, a mechanistic counterpart to the data-driven models. BioSensor-X, a coverage-aware evidence-integration framework for E. coli transcription-factor prioritization, is more peripheral but shares the emphasis on explicit handling of uneven evidence.

ranked.headline: Phosphorylation and condensates remodel ER-plasma membrane contacts and the cortex
ranked.summary: Three preprints and two papers resolve how phosphorylation, phase separation and matrix cues organize cortical and ER-membrane interfaces, including at mitosis and cytokinesis.
ranked.synthesis: The items converge on regulated organization of the cell cortex and ER-plasma membrane interfaces. Mitosis-specific phosphorylation of E-Syt2 drives loss of ER-plasma membrane contact sites, and retaining them delays cell progression. In fission yeast, Pdk1 phosphorylates Pil1 to disassemble eisosomes and remodel plasma membrane and cortical ER at the division site, which is linked to Mid1 recruitment. FRM-4 and FRM-1 phase separate to partition ER-plasma membrane junctions into adjacent calcium-release and calcium-reentry subdomains, and a specialized extracellular matrix (MEC-1, HIM-4/hemicentin) patterns EFA-6 at neuron-epidermis interfaces in C. elegans. MTCL1/2 extend the cytoskeletal theme to the Golgi region, where katanin and CAPZ coordinate microtubules and actin for secretory vesicle docking. New here is mechanistic resolution of kinase-, condensate- and matrix-based control.

ranked.headline: Stem-cell and progenitor platforms are tuned for lineage fidelity and proliferative capacity
ranked.summary: Five preprints advance isogenic, immortalised and pluripotent-derived models of vascular, cardiac and myogenic lineages, with benchmarking of developmental fidelity.
ranked.synthesis: The current items share a focus on building and benchmarking cell models of defined lineages, in cardiovascular and muscle systems. Isogenic hiPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cells compare monosomy-X with euploid lines and reveal donor-specific transcriptomic effects. A single-cell atlas integrating 16 heart organoid datasets benchmarks developmental fidelity across protocols, while a second heart field route yields right ventricular, atrial and left ventricular cardiomyocytes. Two items extend proliferative capacity without transgene integration: CDKN2A knockout by mRNA delivery immortalises non-tumorigenic bovine satellite cells that retain myogenic differentiation, and transient hTERT mRNA adds 2-6 population doublings in Duchenne myogenic progenitors. The new element is the pairing of genetic or protocol control with explicit fidelity or donor-effect readouts. All five are preprints.

ranked.headline: Proteostasis and trafficking modifiers shape amyloid and synuclein toxicity across worm and mouse models
ranked.summary: Five preprints link vesicle trafficking, autophagy and glycan modification to Aβ and α-synuclein pathology, with C. elegans used in two of them.
ranked.synthesis: The current items center on modifiers of protein aggregation and toxicity in neurodegeneration models rather than on lifespan regulation itself. In C. elegans, SV2C protected against MPP+ and paraquat lethality and partly rescued α-synuclein toxicity without restoring motor behavior, while CALM suppressed Aβ aggregation in worms and in vitro. In mice, neuronal CALM loss accelerated plaque formation, neuronal heparan sulfate sulfation promoted α-synuclein uptake and slowed glymphatic clearance, and autophagy deficiency in App knock-in neurons reduced plaques yet worsened cognition and lifespan depending on Aβ burden. A53T α-synuclein overexpression produced sex-dependent striatal LC3 and LAMP1 changes. The common thread is that clearance and trafficking pathways have context-dependent effects; the worm work is limited to toxicity and aggregation readouts, and no item tests the lifespan interventions in the earlier synthesis.

ranked.headline: Long-read and k-mer sequencing resolve mutation rates, parent of origin and difficult regions
ranked.summary: Five preprints apply long-read, methylation and k-mer methods to somatic mutation, mutation spectra, centromeres and benchmarking of difficult genomic regions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is quantifying genomic variation where short-read or reference-based approaches are limited. PacBio HiFi sequencing gives cortical neuron point mutation rates of about 25.9 per diploid genome per year, similar in mice and humans. Context-dependent mutation spectra, with GC-biased gene conversion, are used to model equilibrium trinucleotide composition across 25 plants and 10 mammals. Pooch assigns parent of origin to Hi-C-phased diploid assemblies from differentially methylated CpGs, and cenlen estimates centromere array lengths from short reads in 2,557 1000 Genomes individuals. A stratified HG002 benchmark shows short-read deficits in low-mappability and duplicated regions. New relative to prior material: the focus shifts to centromeres, haplotype assignment and region-stratified accuracy.

ranked.headline: Whole-genome data link phenotypic divergence to geography, gene flow and sorting across taxa
ranked.summary: Five new preprints use genome-scale data to tie phenotypic and lineage divergence to geography, introgression and incomplete lineage sorting in birds, insects, mammals and plants.
ranked.synthesis: The preprints test how phenotypic and lineage divergence arise using whole-genome or multilocus data across owls, butterflies, deer, bromeliads and water voles. Tasmanian masked owls combine larger, darker phenotypes with genomic and niche divergence from mainland birds. Heliconius cydno diversification is linked to Andean geography, and ivory:mir-193 is identified for hindwing band variation. In Old World deer, incomplete lineage sorting dominated Miocene divergences whereas gene flow shaped Pliocene-Pleistocene splits. Puya's Septentrional Clade is proposed as an adaptive radiation tied to paramo expansion. Water voles show divergence near 400 ka and mito-nuclear discordance. What is new is the pairing of phenotypic or ecological patterns with explicit genomic evidence of isolation, introgression and sorting, rather than phenotype-only inference.

ranked.headline: Thylakoid ion antiporters, PsbS protonation and pH biosensors dissect proton control of photoprotection
ranked.summary: Five preprints pair antiporter and PsbS genetics with in vivo pH and metabolite biosensors to resolve how thylakoid proton dynamics tune NPQ.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is how proton and ion fluxes across the thylakoid membrane shape photosynthetic regulation, especially energy-dependent quenching (qE). In Arabidopsis, PsbS mutants with altered lumenal protonation sites show a small zeaxanthin- and acidification-linked quenching, implying complexity in PsbS protonation. NHD1, a thylakoid Na+/H+ antiporter, supports acclimation to fluctuating light and partly overlaps functionally with KEA3 and VCCN1. In Chlamydomonas, KEA3 modulates qE relaxation, including in darkness, and affects growth and low-CO2-induced protein accumulation. New is the pairing of these genetic dissections with in vivo readouts: pHluorin2 was selected among four biosensors to image stromal and lumen pH, and biosensors were combined with chlorophyll fluorescence to link stromal and cytosolic metabolism with photosynthetic function.

ranked.headline: Web, agent and plugin tools make large-scale biological data and simulation analysis more accessible
ranked.summary: Five preprints released 24–25 November describe open platforms and agents for single-cell, cryo-EM and molecular dynamics analysis.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is software that lowers the barrier to analyzing complex biological data, spanning single-cell omics, cryo-EM and molecular simulation. SingloCell offers browser-based exploration of multimodal single-cell data, and CyteArc analyzes remote atlases in place at roughly 100-million-cell scale with provenance tracking. EM-Claw and Molpylot use language-model agents: EM-Claw guides cryo-EM single-particle analysis from accumulated experience, and Molpylot exposes 256 typed tools in a shared human-AI workspace for biomolecular simulation. VMDance brings n-ary similarity clustering and representative selection into VMD as an interactive plugin. The items differ in domain; the dominant emphasis is on implementation: interactivity, reuse, provenance and agent-operable workflows rather than new biological findings.

ranked.headline: Structure, evolution and constrained optimization are tuned to guide protein and enzyme design
ranked.summary: Five preprints probe how evolutionary inputs, benchmarks and optimization constraints determine ML-guided protein engineering outcomes.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is making computational protein design choices explicit and testable. SCOPE integrates structure and evolution in residue-level graph learning to predict enzyme catalytic residues, with mutagenesis validation. A separate study treats MSAs as tunable inputs rather than fixed artifacts, showing that evolutionary information shapes protein generation and folding. A benchmark of 557,143 simulated ML-guided directed evolution campaigns across 16 landscapes finds that design choices transfer poorly between landscapes. GRACE addresses discrete sequence optimization for protein, DNA and RNA under competing constraints using gradients and augmented Lagrangian methods. Structure-guided mining of Zn-His scaffolds combined with small-sample machine learning predicts acetophenone reduction activity. Collectively, the emphasis is on input curation, generalizability and constraint handling, supported by experimental assays in some cases.

ranked.headline: Segmentation and reconstruction tools extend to 3D tissues, cells, nuclei and connectomes
ranked.summary: Five preprints present tools for segmenting, reconstructing and aligning biological structures in 2D and 3D across scales, from nuclei to connectomes.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is computational delineation of biological structures in volumetric or multi-section data, with a growing emphasis on tractable, semi-automated workflows. EpiCycle uses human-in-the-loop iteration for 3D segmentation of stratified epithelia in zebrafish skin, mouse salivary glands and human fetal tissue. A Vaa3D-based platform combines semi-automatic neuronal nucleus segmentation with PCA-based shape analysis and synthetic simulation. A random-walk method probabilistically reconstructs microglia morphology and assigns voxels to cells of origin. Jump provides web tools for exploring and annotating public EM connectomics data such as MICrONS. A benchmark of 15 alignment algorithms for spatial transcriptomics finds no single best method across scenarios, so method choice remains task-dependent.

ranked.headline: Sequence foundation models are adapted and benchmarked for variant effect and regulatory prediction
ranked.summary: Five preprints extend DNA and RNA foundation models to variant scoring, personal epigenomes, lncRNAs and fungal genomes, with benchmarks in LGMD genes.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the adaptation of pretrained sequence models to variant-level or genome-specific prediction tasks. LncRFM extends pretraining to lncRNAs (24.7M sequences) with structure-guided masking; FunDLM does so for 426 fungal genomes, scoring missense and start/stop variants. HapAdapter adds a lightweight adapter so models can infer allele-specific epigenomic effects from diploid personal genomes. A benchmark of six genomic foundation models on 6,960 ClinVar variants in LGMD genes found Evo2 with 501 bp context best, though clinical utility is untested. SpliceVarMech takes a different route, a causal generative framework with Bayesian inference to infer mechanisms of non-canonical splicing variants, evaluated on male infertility genes and BRCA1. Together they shift emphasis from raw scoring toward adaptation, context length and mechanistic interpretation.

ranked.headline: Environmental gradients and stress shape life-history and physiological traits across taxa
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers link elevation, temperature, and early-life stress to measurable differences in growth, metabolism, and development.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how environmental conditions and developmental context shape organismal traits, with local populations and individuals differing in measurable physiology and life-history outcomes. Repeated evolution is examined in deer mice across a gradient of native elevations, and prairie lizards from cool versus warm populations show local adaptations in thermal plasticity that reduce developmental costs at two incubation temperatures. Red-eyed treefrog embryos that hatch early under stress display altered tadpole growth trajectories and transcriptomes, consistent with life-history trade-offs. The avian study is less directly environmental: across 41 phylogenetically controlled species, longer-lived birds show lower routine mitochondrial respiration relative to maximal capacity. What is new is the explicit linkage of trait variation to ecological context across population, individual, and species levels. The designs are comparative and observational, so the items document associations rather than establishing causal mechanisms.

ranked.headline: Mechanical and matrix cues govern vascular and tissue development in mouse and zebrafish
ranked.summary: Recent preprints dissect how flow, matrix proteins and ECM regulators direct vascular and tissue development and remodeling.
ranked.synthesis: The five preprints share a focus on mechanical and matrix-associated cues as determinants of vascular and tissue phenotype, although they differ in system and scope. In mouse neural crest lineages, Tmem2 deletion causes cleft palate with hyaluronan accumulation, hypoxia and vascular defects. Ilk deletion in embryonic renal stroma disrupts fibronectin expression and tissue integrity within a defined developmental window. In zebrafish, hemodynamic forces, klf2a/klf2b and Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent Vegfab-Vegfr2 signaling establish fenestrated endothelial identity in the choroid plexus. Spatial transcriptomics of ductus arteriosus from E14.5 to P2.5 tracks cell-cycle activity and the contractile-to-synthetic transition of mural cells during closure. In atherosclerotic mice, sustained LDL-C lowering expands CD26 and FMOD fibroblast subpopulations with distinct matrix programs, with KLF3 and FOXD1 as candidate regulators. What is new is the extension of this mechanical and matrix logic to ductus arteriosus remodeling and to fibroblast matrix programs during atherosclerosis remodeling.

ranked.headline: Human-specific elements and RHOJ shape progenitor states in developing human cortex
ranked.summary: Single-cell and cross-species multiomics now resolve human-specific regulatory elements that govern cortical progenitor states.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the regulatory logic underlying human-enriched features of cortical development. Locus-resolved long-read profiling in cortical organoids links human-specific transposable elements to the timing of the radial glia-to-neuron transition, tested by CRISPRi manipulation. Cross-species multiomics across human, macaque and mouse fetal cortex identifies RHOJ as an oRG-enriched regulator of human-enriched progenitor states. A single-nucleus accessibility atlas of 1.17M candidate enhancers across 104k mid-gestation human cortical nuclei provides a lineage-restricted regulatory reference. Two further preprints address non-cortical loci: a human-accelerated enhancer contacts FOXC1 and human-specific substitutions boost chondrocyte activity, and parent-of-origin chromatin conformation at Dlk1-Dio3 depends on the germline imprinting control region and can be decoupled from expression. The new element is the combination of locus-resolved perturbation with cross-species and single-nucleus resolution.

ranked.headline: eDNA metabarcoding tracks coral and plankton community change alongside census data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test molecular readouts against conventional census data for coral and plankton communities.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of molecular and community-level data to infer ecological responses in marine and freshwater taxa. Seawater eDNA metabarcoding at Mermaid Reef tracks coral community restructuring after a 2025 heatwave and matches photo-transect cover and assemblage patterns. A 20-year eukaryotic plankton metabarcoding series from the Western English Channel documents a transient 2008-2011 biodiversity shift, while a global comparison across occurrence, abundance, biomass and metagenomic data reports a latitudinal gradient in open-ocean plankton diversity. Two remaining items address different questions: a meta-analysis shows sublethal chemical exposure lowers heat tolerance and increases its variability in freshwater invertebrates and fish, and a comparison of anuran taxonomic and functional diversity contrasts oil-contaminated and reference Choco streams. What is new is the explicit cross-checking of molecular readouts against conventional census methods, most clearly in the coral and plankton studies.

ranked.headline: Multiomic models infer regulatory structure and perturbation effects from single cells
ranked.summary: Single-cell and long-read multiomic data now allow regulatory links to be tested within individual samples and under defined perturbations.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving regulatory relationships at the level of individual cells, samples or interventions rather than population averages. FiberTron trains a compact model on one sample's Fiber-seq and nanopore RNA-seq data to predict base-level chromatin, methylation and transcript patterns and to test regulatory variant effects. In triple-negative breast cancer, a CRISPRi Perturb-seq framework combined with transcription-factor binding priors nominates CTCF, MYC and AP-1 family members as master regulators. CMC-VAE links genes and proteins across CITE-seq data, recovering regulatory structure while interventions refine perturbation predictions. scOnion scores cell-level concordance between paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. GNEval provides a context-specific benchmark of gene associations from 11 single-cell foundation models against Gene Ontology and 14 Perturb-seq datasets. What is new is the use of single-sample multiomic long reads and standardized benchmarking of foundation-model gene networks; all results are preprint-level.

ranked.headline: Somatic mutation profiling expands from plasma cfDNA to mutational processes in tissue
ranked.summary: Plasma cfDNA sequencing and refined mutational-signature methods now probe somatic change in tissues without direct biopsy.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is inferring somatic mutation burden and mutational processes in tissues that are not directly profiled. Two cfDNA preprints report that ultra-sensitive plasma sequencing detects clonal mosaicism in chronic liver disease, with ulcerative colitis also covered for mosaicism. The liver study reports liver-derived somatic mutations with etiology-linked patterns. Systemic sclerosis skin shows widespread somatic mosaicism attributed to ongoing oxidative DNA damage, with C>A burden tracking dcSSc fibrosis severity. The multiple myeloma study extends the repertoire of mutational processes through InDel signatures across 887 whole genomes, identifying a TXNDC5 hotspot and links to treatment outcome. The SEQUENCE method addresses sequence-context bias in signature extraction. The set is heterogeneous: the myeloma and SEQUENCE work concern mutational process inference, while the cfDNA and skin studies concern somatic detection in non-malignant or chronic tissue.

ranked.headline: Selection against deleterious variation shapes genetic load and breeding outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent simulation preprints and a review link deleterious variation to genetic load and breeding gain.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how the distribution of fitness-relevant variation, particularly deleterious alleles, constrains evolutionary and applied outcomes. A review of deleterious mutations covers identification strategies, cross-species variation, evolutionary persistence, and implications for crop breeding and conservation. Forward simulations report that reproductive competition amplifies purifying selection and reduces genetic load more efficiently than the comparison scenario. Individual-based mosquito models show that standing genetic variation evolves under a homing suppression gene drive, altering drive conversion and resistance outcomes. In admixed crop germplasm, simulations show that low founder isoeliteness reduces genomic selection gain, and an isoeliteness-guided method is proposed to address this. The gene drive and genomic selection items extend the thread beyond load alone, so it describes the dominant theme rather than every item. Most evidence is simulation-based or preprint-stage.

ranked.headline: Regulatory and coding changes underlie convergent and divergent trait evolution
ranked.summary: Long-read avian genomes, Xiphophorus pigmentation and acorn worm single-cell data test how regulatory and coding changes shape trait diversity.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how genetic and regulatory changes across lineages and human populations map onto trait variation. In Xiphophorus evelynae, the confetti caudal tail-spotting phenotype shares an xmrk-linked genetic basis with tailspots in other species, indicating convergent molecular evolution of a cancer-associated pigmentation trait. Comparative analysis of long-read avian genomes links independent origins of behavioral innovation to positive selection and constrained regulatory evolution. In Saccoglossus kowalevskii, single-cell RNA-seq shows that neuronal cell types diverge widely across animal phyla around a shared core of neuronal genes. A human preprint intersects ancestral and hominin-derived variants with ClinVar, gnomAD and GTEx, reporting cerebellum-linked expression differences. What is new is the joint use of lineage-level comparative data and population or clinical resources to ask which evolutionary changes in regulation and coding underlie phenotypic diversity.

ranked.headline: Drosophila traits respond to selection, diet and genetic perturbation in distinct ways
ranked.summary: Recent Drosophila preprints link artificial selection, diet and gene disruption to sleep, lifespan and recombination phenotypes.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints examine how selection, genetic background and nutrition shape phenotypic responses in Drosophila melanogaster, with sex-specific effects recurring across them. Artificially selected early and late eclosion chronotype lines show correlated divergence in sleep architecture, fragmentation and recovery. Disrupting the ecdysone oxidase gene fezzik alters transcription, metabolism, L-dopa levels and sex-specific lifespan, with chinmo implicated in female effects. Experimental evolution under yeast deprivation detected no change in male fitness components, suggesting that nutrient-driven adaptation is female-specific. DGRP lines on varying caloric diets show genotype-dependent plasticity in X-chromosome recombination that is not associated with survival or fecundity. Taken together, the items suggest that trait responses can be decoupled from fitness readouts and are often sex-specific, although the studies address distinct traits and do not share a single mechanism.

ranked.headline: Transposable elements drive structural and expression variation across crop genomes
ranked.summary: Chromosome-scale and pangenome assemblies in wheat, maize, rice and a fungal pathogen now resolve transposable element-driven variation at haplotype and cultivar levels.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is structural variation in genome assemblies, with transposable elements (TEs) as a recurring driver. In bread wheat, cultivar-specific TE insertions within gene bodies track homoeolog expression bias, mainly through suppression of one homoeolog, linking TE polymorphism to expression dominance. In the maize pangenome graph of 58 assemblies, TEs generate structural complexity, and Tajima's D analyses suggest that complex regions are maintained polymorphisms rather than neutral noise. Chromosome-scale, haplotype-resolved assemblies extend this framework to the heterokaryotic fungal pathogen Rhizoctonia solani AG1-IB, whose haplotypes share ~97.75% identity, and to the Hattan sake-rice lineage, where a genomic mosaic with local variation is described. The new element is the resolution of haplotype- and cultivar-level structure at chromosome scale across these systems.

ranked.headline: Cognitive load and resource state reshape decision-related neural network dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link state-dependent decision and communication dynamics to distributed prefrontal, parietal and striatal circuits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that decision and attention variables are carried by state-dependent network interactions rather than fixed regional responses. In a human fMRI bandit task, working-memory load reduced directed exploration and reconfigured aIns-IPS coupling. In rhesus monkeys, prefrontal neurons in ACC, OFC and DLPFC encoded and updated value according to the resource state of an earning-spending task. Graphical Ising models fitted to OFC spike data indicate that offer values shift network attractors toward relative-value choice states. Communication subspaces spanning prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate and caudate emerge before gaze-directed object selection and develop with learning. What is new across these preprints is the joint use of state-dependent measures and reduced network descriptions, applied to exploration, valuation, choice and attentional selection across human and primate recordings.

ranked.headline: New E3 ligase recruiters (DCAF10, FBXO22, FBXO31) drive targeted protein degradation
ranked.summary: Four preprints report new E3 ligase recruiters for targeted degradation and a PP2A-B55 mechanism that terminates Parkin-dependent mitophagy.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across three preprints is the use of small-molecule recruiters to redirect specific E3 ligases toward target proteins for degradation, including FKBP12, BRD9 and BRD4. DCAF10 is identified as a targeted protein degradation E3 ligase, and an Ac-GFG-based recruiter, optimized to Pr-GFI, degrades FKBP12 and BRD9 in a DCAF10-dependent manner. FBXO22 is recruited through a quantum-mechanics-guided covalent warhead conjugated to JQ1, which acts as a molecular glue degrader of BRD4. Indoline-2-carboxamide recruiters engage FBXO31, with lead JZ26 degrading FKBP12 at endogenous levels (DC50 2.5 nM). The new element is rational, interface-aware recruiter design extended to additional E3 ligases. The PP2A-B55α preprint is mechanistically distinct: a non-canonical B55 interface binds the folded Parkin Ubl domain to dephosphorylate pParkin and terminate PINK1-Parkin mitophagy, linking it to the same theme of selective control of protein-protein interfaces.

ranked.headline: Integrative methods map protein ligands and targets of small molecules
ranked.summary: Four recent preprints apply metabolomics, in silico, AI-guided, and HDX-MS approaches to resolve protein interactions in complex systems.
ranked.synthesis: Across these preprints, the dominant thread is the mapping of molecular interactions under conditions that extend beyond purified components. A metabolomics workflow combining HPLC fractionation with STD NMR aims to identify endogenous low-affinity metabolite ligands of fructosamine-3-kinase, while an integrative in silico pipeline with transcriptomics and structural bioinformatics nominates 27 putative human protein targets of plastic-derived chemicals. An AI agent-guided pipeline reports a small molecule that disrupts LAG-3 interactions with tau and amyloid-beta while sparing MHC II and FGL1. Crude-HDX extends hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry from purified proteins to lysates and intact cells, applied to KRAS and SOScat. The new element is the shift toward target and ligand discovery in native or crowded cellular contexts. The items are heterogeneous, with computational and experimental approaches differing in scope and maturity.

ranked.headline: Nascent RNA architecture and Argonaute networks shape post-transcriptional control
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend RNA fate, nascent transcript localization, LTR chromatin and Argonaute network analyses across model systems.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how RNA processing, spatial organization and chromatin engagement determine gene expression output. A full-length capped RNA study in mouse embryonic stem cells connects exosome surveillance of PROMPTs and transcript architecture to RNA fate and regulatory state. In Drosophila spermatocytes, nascent kl-3 transcripts show spatial segregation of exonic and intronic RNA on the Y-loop, with Smooth protein required for this organization. In mouse and human pluripotent stem cells, SMARCA4 preferentially occupies lineage-specific LTR retrotransposons co-bound by POU5F1 and SOX2, linking repeat elements to chromatin regulatory architecture. Argonomics Explorer provides a searchable resource for comparing Argonaute-sRNA and AGO-target interactions across public small RNA datasets. What is new is the resolution of transcript architecture and spatial RNA localization at the level of individual loci, together with repeat-element engagement by pluripotency factors.

ranked.headline: Membrane binding modes and bilayer defects of lipid-associated proteins
ranked.summary: Simulations and in vivo assays now resolve how proteins distort bilayers to bind membranes and assemble into oligomers.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints converge on how proteins engage lipid bilayers through membrane perturbation and interface-specific contacts. Molecular dynamics simulations of 13 plant lipid droplet proteins, combined with in vivo tobacco pollen tube assays, identify distinct membrane binding modes, including binding via a hydrophobic face. Coarse-grained simulations of ten channels and transporters in POPC bilayers reveal membrane defects at oligomeric interfaces that may drive lipid-mediated oligomerization. A new Python package, MembraneCurvature, built on MDAnalysis, computes membrane curvature from simulation trajectories. Biophysical characterization of the yeast Osh4 ALPS-like motif, using CD, fluorescence, ITC, XRD and MD simulations, shows preferential binding to anionic TGN membranes. The new elements are the comparison of binding modes across lipid droplet proteins and the framing of oligomeric interfaces in terms of membrane defects.

ranked.headline: Noninvasive stimulation and neurofeedback modulate human cortical excitation-inhibition
ranked.summary: Recent human preprints test whether EEG aperiodic slope, TMS-EEG responses and slow waves index cortical excitation-inhibition balance non-invasively.
ranked.synthesis: Four recent preprints address whether non-invasive measures of cortical excitation-inhibition balance can be read out and manipulated in humans. The dominant thread is the EEG and MEG aperiodic 1/f slope as a proxy for this balance. Closed-loop neurofeedback volitionally modulated the sensorimotor slope, with steeper states associated with reduced motor cortex TMS responses. In children aged 10-18, the MEG exponent tracked parietal-occipital GABA+ levels in typically developing participants but not in autism. Two stimulation studies extend this framing: 1 Hz transcranial temporal interference increased NREM slow-wave density, and prolonged intermittent theta burst stimulation altered left frontal theta responses in a sham-controlled crossover TMS-EEG design. The new element is the joint use of aperiodic readouts, deep-target stimulation and TMS-EEG within one excitation-inhibition framework.

ranked.headline: Brain network dynamics track perception, learning and clinical phenotypes
ranked.summary: Four preprints apply dynamic connectivity, optimal transport and tensor methods to EEG, MEG and fMRI data from humans.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints share a focus on how brain activity is organised over time and across regions, rather than on static activation. A dynamic causal model of EEG during breaking continuous flash suppression links top-down prefrontal connectivity to perceptual breakthrough. A Gaussian hidden Markov model combined with optimal transport, applied to resting-state fMRI from 122 multiple sclerosis patients and 97 controls, yields patient subgroups with distinct brain dynamics. Tensor decomposition of OP-MEG data from three epilepsy patients recovers motor beta and visual alpha components, establishing feasibility. Multimodal eye-tracking, pupillometry and EEG during naturalistic learning in 86 participants show that brain-body state dynamics predict subsequent quiz performance. The novelty lies in applying time-resolved, multimodal decomposition to clinical stratification and to learning outcomes.

ranked.headline: LEC input, spine shrinkage and CA1 firing shape hippocampal plasticity and recall
ranked.summary: Recent preprints dissect activity-dependent synaptic and firing changes in hippocampal circuits that underlie memory recall and plasticity.
ranked.synthesis: These preprints converge on activity-dependent control of hippocampal synaptic strength and firing as a substrate of memory. In CA1, glutamatergic input from the lateral entorhinal cortex rises during object and Barnes maze recall, silencing this pathway impairs recall, and optogenetic input induces LTP. Persistent dendritic spine shrinkage during mGluR-induced LTD depends on coincident neuronal activity. At hippocampal mossy fiber synapses, GABAB-receptor presynaptic inhibition shifts transmission from detonation to subdetonation mode and limits vesicle pool plasticity. Blocking translation in dorsal CA1 pyramidal cells impairs novelty-induced increases in population firing while preserving sharp-wave ripple reactivation of newly formed assemblies. The distinctive contribution is the dissociation of firing-rate gain from assembly formation, together with the requirement for neuronal activity in gating structural LTD.

ranked.headline: Robust Brain Network Mapping and Receptor-Linked Connectivity Changes in Preprints
ranked.summary: Recent preprints target the reliability of brain network estimates and link connectivity changes to E/I balance, microglia and receptor maps.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is anchoring regional brain measures to network-level and molecular organization. GROW introduces a cluster-growing framework for functional coordinate network mapping aimed at improving the robustness of Alzheimer's disease brain network maps. In people at clinical high risk for psychosis, resting-state fMRI Hurst exponent reductions are linked to excitation/inhibition balance and receptor distributions, with preliminary findings. A single-woman longitudinal MRI study maps pregnancy-related cortical gray matter loss onto cognitive and neurotransmitter receptor maps. Public human single-nucleus data show sparse adrenergic receptor detection in microglia and an age-linked shift from homeostatic to inflammatory hippocampal microglia. This thread is not shared by all items: GROW is primarily methodological, and the microglia study rests on sparse detection in public data. What is new is the explicit pairing of imaging or transcriptomic readouts with receptor-level biology.

ranked.headline: Software tools advance microbiome, metaproteomic and barcoding sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Four 2026 preprints add agentic, database, web-based and nanopore tools for microbiome sequence and proteomic analysis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is tool-level development for microbial sequence and proteomic analysis, with emphasis on automation, reference resources and accessible deployment. MicroBioAgent proposes an autonomous AI agent that builds and runs adaptive pipelines for 16S, shotgun and de novo metagenomic analysis. RADSuite pairs RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, with RADx, which identifies V regions to enable species-level microbiome identification. Unipept's 2026 update moves multi-sample metaproteomics, including project organization, comparison and pathway mapping, into a web platform. ONTOLOGY offers a GUI-driven workflow with freeze-dried PCR plates and two pipelines for nanopore DNA barcoding and metabarcoding, aimed at decentralized use. Together these preprints address workflow design, taxonomic resolution and usability rather than reporting new biological findings. The novelty lies in combining curated reference data, agent-based automation and point-of-use access within analysis pipelines.
